meta.title: Export, Import & Back Up Bookmarks – Chrome Extension | Snug
meta.description: Snug is a Chrome extension that exports, imports and backs up your bookmarks, with scheduled backups. It needs no account and makes no network calls.

seo.ogImageAlt: Snug logo, an amber bookmark icon, above a short summary of the extension on a dark background.

hero.subheadline: Snug exports, imports and backs up your bookmarks in Chrome and other Chromium browsers. It makes no network calls and needs no account.
hero.note: Free. Open source. Works in Chrome, Edge, Brave and Opera.

journey.description: Your bookmarks leave your browser as one bookmarks.html file, available in six formats, and open in another browser. All of it stays on your device.

trust.heading: An extension that has no server to trust
trust.intro: Snug reads and writes your browser's own bookmarks tree, on your device. It never connects to anything, so there is nowhere for your bookmarks to go.

network.title: No network calls
network.body: Snug makes none. Every export and import happens locally.

account.title: No account
account.body: There is nothing to sign up for and nothing to log in to.

source.title: Open source
source.body: The code is public. Read it, or check the project's OpenSSF Scorecard and Best Practices badges, CodeQL scans and CI runs.

trust.access: Reading and writing your bookmarks is the only way an extension can export and import them. Snug does that and nothing else.

export.title: Export what you choose
export.body: Export the whole tree or only the folders you pick, as HTML, JSON, CSV, Markdown, OPML or XBEL. Filenames can include the date, so you can tell them apart later.

preview.title: Preview before you import
preview.body: Import HTML, JSON, CSV or XBEL files, a Chrome profile “Bookmarks” file, or a Safari export with Favorites and Reading List, several files at once if you like. Snug detects the format and previews what will be added, skipped and deleted. Then you merge, replace, or add everything to a new folder. When you merge or add to a new folder, you can uncheck any folder or bookmark first.

undo.title: Undo a replace
undo.body: Replace saves a Safety snapshot first. Snug keeps the latest five, and you can restore any of them from Settings.

duplicates.title: Clean up duplicates
duplicates.body: A Duplicates page finds repeated bookmarks. On import, Skip duplicates leaves out URLs you already have.

backup.title: Back up on a schedule
backup.body: Auto-export saves your bookmarks to the Downloads folder on a schedule you set. Retention keeps only the newest files, and you can get a notification if a run fails.

works.title: Works where you are
works.body: Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera and other Chromium browsers. The interface comes in 10 languages and follows your browser's theme and language.

network.question: Does Snug send my bookmarks anywhere?
network.answer: No. Snug makes no network calls. It reads and writes your browser's bookmarks on your device, and the source code is public so you can check.

account.question: Do I need an account?
account.answer: No. Install it and start exporting.

sync.question: Does it sync my bookmarks between devices?
sync.answer: No. Snug has no sync and no cloud. To move bookmarks to another browser or computer, export a file and import it there.

oneFile.question: Can I import several files at once?
oneFile.answer: Yes. Pick or drop several files on the Import page or in the toolbar popup and Snug imports them in one go.

permissions.question: Why does it need access to all my bookmarks?
permissions.answer: Reading and writing them is the only way an extension can export and import them. Snug makes no network calls, so nothing it reads can leave your device.

builtin.question: My browser already exports HTML. Why use Snug?
builtin.answer: The built-in export has no folder selection, preview, undo, schedule, duplicate check or extra formats. Snug has all of them.

overwrite.question: Will it overwrite my current bookmarks?
overwrite.answer: Only if you choose Replace. You see a preview first, and Replace saves a Safety snapshot you can restore.

formats.question: Which formats does it handle?
formats.answer: Export as HTML, JSON, CSV, Markdown, OPML or XBEL. Import HTML, JSON, CSV or XBEL, a Chrome profile “Bookmarks” file, or a Safari export.

browsers.question: Which browsers does it work in?
browsers.answer: Chrome and other Chromium browsers such as Edge, Brave and Opera.

safe.question: Is it safe to install a solo developer's extension?
safe.answer: The source is public, CodeQL scans it, the project has OpenSSF Scorecard and Best Practices badges, and CI runs pinned. Judge it yourself on GitHub.

final.heading: Take your bookmarks with you
final.line: Add Snug to Chrome and export, import or back up in a few clicks. Free, open source, and nothing leaves your device.

footer.note: Snug is open source under the MIT license.

meta.title: Privacy Policy | Snug
meta.description: How Snug handles your data: the extension sends nothing anywhere, and this website uses cookieless analytics.

notice.body: This page is an AI translation that no person has reviewed. If it differs from the English version, the English version prevails.

website.heading: This website
website.body: The extension sends nothing anywhere. This website measures visits with Umami Cloud, a cookieless analytics service that processes the data for us.

collected.pageviews: Pageviews and the page that referred the visitor
collected.environment: Browser, operating system and device type
collected.country: Country, taken from the request and not stored as an IP address
collected.clicks: Clicks on install buttons, reviews, the video, FAQ questions, the language and theme switchers, and outbound links

website.noCookies: Umami sets no cookies and stores nothing in your browser. It respects Do Not Track: if your browser sends it, you are not counted.
website.logs: The web server also keeps an access log with the time, the requested page, the status, the referer and your browser's user-agent. IP addresses are masked in that log, and it is read offline.

privacy.theme: Your theme choice is stored only in your browser.
